= Karpenter Provider Oxide
:description: Karpenter node provisioning for Oxide.
:p: oxide-karpenter
:anchor_prefix: k8s-api

[.lead]
Karpenter Provider Oxide launches Kubernetes nodes on an Oxide rack.

`OxideNodeClass` describes the Oxide-specific configuration used by a Karpenter `NodePool`, including bootstrap, image and subnet selection, storage, SSH keys, external IPs, and affinity.

NOTE: The provider API is currently `karpenter.oxide.computer/v1alpha1`.
Treat compatibility guarantees accordingly.

[id="oxide-node-class"]
== OxideNodeClass

Reference an `OxideNodeClass` from `spec.template.spec.nodeClassRef` on a Karpenter `NodePool`.
The selected image, subnet, and other Oxide resources must already exist.

[source,yaml]
----
apiVersion: karpenter.oxide.computer/v1alpha1
kind: OxideNodeClass
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  storage:
    boot:
      size: 20Gi
  kubeletArgs:
    - cloud-provider=external
  bootstrap:
    rke2:
      tokenRef:
        name: rancher-agent-token
        namespace: kube-system
        key: token
  imageSelector:
    - name: rke2-ubuntu-*
      project: my-project
  subnetSelector:
    - vpcName: default
      project: my-project
----

Selectors resolve existing Oxide resources; where a selector matches multiple images, the most recently uploaded image is used.
Leave `server` unset to discover the Kubernetes API endpoint from the `default/kubernetes` EndpointSlice.
Exactly one bootstrap provider, `rke2` or `kubeadm`, must be configured.

See xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassspec[OxideNodeClassSpec] for every field, default, and validation rule.

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinity"]
==== Affinity



Affinity controls which Oxide affinity and anti-affinity groups launched instances join.

Selected groups are referenced only: Karpenter adds its instances to them, removes its instances
from them, and never creates, updates or deletes the groups themselves.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassspec[$$OxideNodeClassSpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`affinityGroupSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinitygroupselector[$$AffinityGroupSelector$$] array__ | AffinityGroupSelector selects existing affinity groups that every launched instance joins. +
Affinity groups are an experimental Oxide API. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason AntiAffinityGroupSelector is. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`antiAffinityGroupSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinitygroupselector[$$AffinityGroupSelector$$] array__ | AntiAffinityGroupSelector selects existing anti-affinity groups that every launched instance +
joins. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash because whether nodes are replaced when this changes is +
decided by comparing resolved groups, not by hashing the spec: a selector rewritten to name +
the group it already matched has changed nothing about where an instance sits. See IsDrifted. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`managed`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-managedaffinitygroup[$$ManagedAffinityGroup$$]__ | Managed asks Karpenter to own one group for this nodeclass that every launched instance joins. +
It is created when the nodeclass is reconciled and deleted when the nodeclass is. Its name is +
derived from the nodeclass name and from the fields below, so that changing either produces a +
new group rather than an edit the Oxide API cannot make. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason the selectors are: whether nodes are +
replaced when this changes is decided by comparing resolved groups, not by hashing the spec. +
A hash cannot tell a group being added from one being removed, and only the first replaces +
nodes. See IsDrifted. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===


[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinitygroupselector"]
==== AffinityGroupSelector



AffinityGroupSelector selects affinity or anti-affinity groups by ID or by name.

Deliberately without CEL requiring exactly one of id/name, matching ImageSelector and the rest of
the selectors, which validate at reconcile instead.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinity[$$Affinity$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`id`* __string__ | ID is the exact group UUID. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`name`* __string__ | Name is the name of a group. A name without a "*" must match exactly, ignoring case. +

A name containing "*" selects every group whose name matches, where each "*" stands for any +
run of characters including none. So "karpenter-*" selects both "karpenter-spread-a" and +
"karpenter-spread-b". +

Unlike an image selector, where a wildcard picks a single winner, every matching group is +
joined. A wildcard therefore makes the set of groups a function of the project's contents +
rather than of the nodeclass alone: a group created in the project whose name matches an +
existing selector joins the set, and because an instance can only join a group at launch, +
every node then drifts and is replaced so it can join. That is a fleet replacement triggered +
from outside Kubernetes. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-diskset"]
==== DiskSet



DiskSet is a group of identically configured disks attached to every launched instance.

mountPath and mountDir are two mutually exclusive fields rather than one field with two meanings.
mountPath is a literal mount point; mountDir is a parent directory, and disk k lands at
<mountDir>/<name>-<k>. Naming the two cases is what makes the incoherent combination
unrepresentable: the local static provisioner discovers the *contents* of its hostDir, so a
hostDir that is itself a symlink to a raw block device discovers nothing. It also means there is
no discontinuity in what a path means as count grows from one to two.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-storage[$$Storage$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`name`* __string__ | Name identifies the set. It appears in the disk names Karpenter creates and in the directory +
each disk is mounted under, so it is constrained to what is legal in both. +

The minimum of three characters is not cosmetic. It is what makes every disk name at least 20 +
bytes long, and 20 bytes is exactly what the guest sees of a disk name as its NVMe serial +
number. A shorter name would be padded by the NVMe layer, which the guest would then have to +
know to strip. See pkg/providers/storage. + |  | MaxLength: 20 +
MinLength: 3 +
Pattern: `^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$` +

| *`type`* __string__ | Type is whether the set's disks are Distributed, replicated across the rack by Crucible and +
able to outlive the sled, or Local, sitting on the sled the instance is placed on. +

Local disks have a fixed 4 KiB block size, cannot be created from an image or a snapshot, and +
do not outlive the instance. They are also provisioned differently: a local disk's capacity +
belongs to one sled, so it is created by the instance create itself rather than ahead of it. +
See pkg/providers/instance. + | Distributed | Enum: [Distributed Local] +

| *`count`* __integer__ | Count is how many disks the set has. Every disk in the set has the same size, type, source and +
filesystem; what differs is where it is mounted. + | 1 | Maximum: 7 +
Minimum: 1 +
Optional: \{} +

| *`size`* __link:https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#quantity-resource-api[$$Quantity$$]__ | Size is the capacity of each disk in the set, not of the set as a whole. A set of four 500Gi +
disks provisions 2Ti. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`layout`* __string__ | Layout is how the set's disks are presented to the guest. Individual, the only value, gives one +
filesystem per disk, which is what the local static provisioner consumes. + | Individual | Enum: [Individual] +
Optional: \{} +

| *`filesystem`* __string__ | Filesystem is what the guest formats each disk with. None leaves the disk as a raw block +
device: nothing is created on it and nothing is mounted, which is what a +
consumer that manages its own on-disk format wants. +

Deliberately without a CRD default even though an unset filesystem means ext4. A default +
applies unconditionally, and a disk created from an image or a snapshot must never be +
formatted, so a defaulted ext4 would be an instruction to destroy the image the user asked +
for, and CRDs have no conditional default. Unset is therefore resolved to ext4 only where +
formatting is meaningful, and the effective value is published on the status so it is still +
readable off the object. + |  | Enum: [ext4 xfs None] +
Optional: \{} +

| *`mountPath`* __string__ | MountPath is the single mount point for a set of one disk. Mutually exclusive with MountDir. + |  | MaxLength: 253 +
Pattern: `^/[^/]+(/[^/]+)*$` +
Optional: \{} +

| *`mountDir`* __string__ | MountDir is the parent directory the set's disks are placed beneath: disk k is mounted at +
<mountDir>/<name>-<k>, counting from zero, or for a raw block set is linked there instead. +
That is the layout the local static provisioner's hostDir expects. Mutually exclusive with +
MountPath. + |  | MaxLength: 253 +
Pattern: `^/[^/]+(/[^/]+)*$` +
Optional: \{} +

| *`imageSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-imageselector[$$ImageSelector$$] array__ | ImageSelector selects the image each disk in the set is created from. Only for Distributed +
sets: the Oxide API has no disk source for a local disk at all. +

Resolved per set, so two sets carrying the same selector resolve once between them. A set whose +
selector matches nothing holds the nodeclass un-Ready rather than launching a disk with an +
empty source. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the reason every selector is: what it matches is a +
function of the project as well as of the nodeclass, so its drift is decided by comparing +
resolved state. Excluded by storageFingerprint simply not covering it, rather than by a tag, +
which at this depth would do nothing. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`snapshotSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-snapshotselector[$$SnapshotSelector$$] array__ | SnapshotSelector selects the snapshot each disk in the set is created from. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason ImageSelector is. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`readOnly`* __boolean__ | ReadOnly asks the rack to attach the disks read-only, which is only meaningful for a disk +
created from an image or a snapshot. It is a property of the attachment rather than of the +
guest's mount: the guest cannot write to it whatever it does with the mount options. +

Note that the disks of a set are still deleted with the node. A snapshot-sourced set reads +
like "restore this dataset onto every node", and the per-node copy does not outlive the node. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===

set with a filesystem. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`images`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxideimage[$$OxideImage$$] array__ | Images and Snapshots are the resolved sources, most recent first and truncated the same way +
Status.Images is. Only the first is ever used; the rest are reported so a wildcard selector can +

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-ephemeralip"]
==== EphemeralIP



EphemeralIP is one external address attached to an instance at launch.

The two fields are the two ways Oxide's PoolSelector can name a pool, and at least one is
required: ipVersion alone is PoolSelectorAuto, which takes the silo's default pool for that
version; pool alone is PoolSelectorExplicit. Setting both is allowed and is checked for
agreement when the nodeclass is reconciled, since only the resolved pool knows its version.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassspec[$$OxideNodeClassSpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`ipVersion`* __string__ | IPVersion is the address family this entry allocates. + |  | Enum: [v4 v6] +
Optional: \{} +

| *`pool`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-ippoolref[$$IPPoolRef$$]__ | Pool is the IP pool to allocate from. When unset the silo's default pool for ipVersion is +
used. A pool is linked to a silo rather than owned by a project, so no project is named. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===




[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-ippoolref"]
==== IPPoolRef



IPPoolRef identifies exactly one IP pool. Unlike the image and subnet selectors it is a
reference rather than a selector: the number of ephemeral addresses an instance gets is fixed by
the nodeclass, so a reference matching two pools is an error rather than two addresses.

| *`name`* __string__ | Name is the exact name of an IP pool. No wildcards: a reference resolves to one pool. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`id`* __string__ | ID is the exact image UUID + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`name`* __string__ | Name is the name of an image. A name without a "*" must match exactly, ignoring case. +

A name containing "*" selects every image whose name matches, where each "*" stands for any +
run of characters including none. So "rke2-ubuntu-*" and "rke2-*" both select +
"rke2-ubuntu-1780929039", and "*-ubuntu-*" selects it as well. Unlike a version, a name is +
matched character by character, so a wildcard does not have to fall on a "-" boundary. +

When a wildcard matches several images the most recently uploaded one is launched. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`project`* __string__ | Project where the image is located. +
If the project is not specified, then we query for Silo level images +
that are not linked to a project. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`os`* __string__ | OS is the operating system of the image + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`version`* __string__ | Version is the version of the image or OS. Oxide image versions are free-form, so a version +
without a "*" is matched literally and case-insensitively. +

A version containing "*" is instead matched a segment at a time, where segments are separated +
by ".", "-", "_", or whitespace, and a leading "v" is ignored on both sides. A "*" matches +
exactly one segment, except as the last segment of the version, where it matches one or more +
remaining segments. So "1.2.*" selects "1.2.3" but not "1.2" or "1.20"; "1.*" selects both +
"1.4" and "1.4.2"; and "24.04 *" selects "24.04 2026-05-09". +

When a wildcard matches several images the most recently uploaded one is launched. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===

survive until the node completes TLS bootstrap, so this should stay short. + | 15m | Optional: \{} +

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-managedaffinitygroup"]
==== ManagedAffinityGroup



ManagedAffinityGroup is the single group Karpenter owns end to end for a nodeclass.

Being a single pointer with a Type enum is what structurally enforces one managed group per
nodeclass, with no CEL needed. Both its fields are mutable, and changing either creates a
different group: the Oxide API cannot patch a group's policy or its kind, so a successor has to
be creatable while the predecessor still exists, which is why the name encodes both.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinity[$$Affinity$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`type`* __string__ | Type is whether the managed group co-locates instances on a sled (Affinity) or spreads them +
across sleds (AntiAffinity). Affinity groups are an experimental Oxide API. + |  | Enum: [Affinity AntiAffinity] +

| *`policy`* __string__ | Policy is what the rack does when the request cannot be satisfied. Allow places the instance +
anyway; fail refuses the launch, which is a hazard worth opting into rather than defaulting +
to, since a refusal for want of a satisfiable placement is not a refusal any smaller instance +
shape would avoid. + | allow | Enum: [allow fail] +
Optional: \{} +

|===


[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxideaffinitygroup"]

OxideAffinityGroup is one resolved Oxide affinity or anti-affinity group.

| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`id`* __string__ |  |  | 
| *`name`* __string__ | Name is the group's name at the time it resolved. The ID is the identity: a group deleted and +
recreated under the same name is a different group that the running instances are not members +
of, and comparing IDs is what makes that visible. + |  | 
| *`type`* __string__ | Type is Affinity or AntiAffinity, which is also which Oxide endpoint the group is reached on. + |  | 
| *`policy`* __string__ | Policy is what the rack does when the group's constraint cannot be satisfied, allow or fail. + |  | 
| *`managed`* __boolean__ | Managed marks the one group Karpenter owns for this nodeclass, and so the only one it will +

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassspec"]
==== OxideNodeClassSpec



OxideNodeClassSpec is the top level specification for the Oxide Karpenter Provider.
This will contain configuration necessary to launch instances on Oxide.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclass[$$OxideNodeClass$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`userData`* __string__ | UserData to be applied to the provisioned nodes. +
It must be in the appropriate format based on the machine image in use. Karpenter will merge certain fields into +
this UserData to ensure nodes are being provisioned with the correct configuration. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`env`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-envvar[$$EnvVar$$] array__ |  |  | 
| *`server`* __string__ | Server is the endpoint nodes use to join the cluster. When empty it is discovered from the +
default/kubernetes EndpointSlice. Each bootstrap provider renders the discovered address in +
the form it needs, so the port differs by provider: RKE2 joins on the supervisor port (9345) +
while kubeadm joins on the kube-apiserver port (6443). + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`kubeletArgs`* __string array__ | KubeletArgs are extra kubelet arguments in "key=value" form applied to launched nodes, +
in addition to the args Karpenter requires. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`bootstrap`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-bootstrap[$$Bootstrap$$]__ | Bootstrap selects and configures the mechanism nodes use to join the cluster. +
Exactly one provider may be set. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`imageSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-imageselector[$$ImageSelector$$] array__ | ImageSelector is used to select an image to launch nodes with. +
If multiple images match then the most recently uploaded image is selected. +
Selectors are OR'd together, but terms within a selector are AND'd together +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the reason every selector is: what a selector matches is a +
function of the project as well as of the nodeclass, so drift is decided by comparing resolved +
state rather than by hashing the terms. A selector rewritten to name the image it already +
matched has changed nothing about the running nodes, and a new image uploaded into an unchanged +
wildcard has. See IsDrifted. + |  | 
| *`storage`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-storage[$$Storage$$]__ | Storage is the disks every instance launched from this nodeclass is created with: the boot +
disk, and any additional sets of data disks. +

A value rather than a pointer, and required: a nodeclass has always needed a boot disk size, +
so making the whole stanza optional would buy nothing but a nil check in every reader. +

Everything here except the nested source selectors is fixed into an instance at launch: a disk +
cannot be resized, re-sourced or re-mounted afterwards, so a change to any of it is +
drift by definition. +

Excluded from the reflected part of the nodeclass hash all the same, and folded in as an +
explicit fingerprint instead. Reflection cannot be used here because the sizes are +
resource.Quantity, which keeps its value in unexported fields and its formatting in an exported +
one, so a reflected hash would see how a size was written rather than what it is. Tagging the +
individual sizes does not work either: hashstructure only honours hash:"ignore" on fields of the +
struct it is handed, not on fields of structs nested inside it, so a tag down here would be +
silently ineffective. See Hash and storageFingerprint. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`subnetSelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-subnetselector[$$SubnetSelector$$] array__ | SubnetSelector is used to select subnets to launch nodes into. +
Multiple subnets can match. Node launches will use subnets with available IP space. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason ImageSelector is. + |  | 
| *`sshKeySelector`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-sshkeyselector[$$SSHKeySelector$$] array__ | SSHKeySelector is used to select SSH keys that will be copied to the node +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason ImageSelector is. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`ephemeralIPs`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-ephemeralip[$$EphemeralIP$$] array__ | EphemeralIPs are the external addresses attached to every launched instance. An ephemeral +
address is allocated when the instance is created and released when it is destroyed. +

Oxide allows at most one ephemeral address per IP version, so at most two entries, and the +
versions must differ. Unset means launched nodes get no external address. +

Excluded from the nodeclass hash for the same reason ImageSelector is: what a pool reference +
resolves to is a function of the silo as well as of the nodeclass, so drift is decided by +
comparing resolved pools rather than by hashing the spec. + |  | MaxItems: 2 +
Optional: \{} +

| *`affinity`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-affinity[$$Affinity$$]__ | Affinity controls which Oxide affinity and anti-affinity groups launched instances join. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===


[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassstatus"]
==== OxideNodeClassStatus



OxideNodeClassStatus contains the resolved state of the OxideNodeClass



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclass[$$OxideNodeClass$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`server`* __string__ | Server is the user-defined or system discovered endpoint that nodes will use to join the cluster. +
It is rendered by the configured bootstrap provider, so its form and port are provider-specific. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`kubeletArgs`* __string array__ | KubeletArgs contain user-defined and system default kubelet args that are applied to launched nodes + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`nodeTaints`* __string array__ | NodeTaints contain user-defined and system default node taints that are applied to launched nodes + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`images`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxideimage[$$OxideImage$$] array__ | Images contain selected images to use for the boot disk of launched nodes, most recently +
uploaded first. Nodes always launch with the first entry; the remaining entries are the +
runners-up a wildcard version selector also matched, and are reported only so the selection +
can be understood. The list is truncated, so it is not necessarily every match. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`subnets`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidesubnet[$$OxideSubnet$$] array__ | Subnets contain selected subnets for launching nodes into + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`sshKeys`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidesshkey[$$OxideSSHKey$$] array__ | SSHKeys contain selected ssh keys to copy to launched nodes + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`ephemeralIPs`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxideephemeralip[$$OxideEphemeralIP$$] array__ | EphemeralIPs contain the resolved pool each launched instance takes an external address from, +
in the order spec.ephemeralIPs declares them. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`affinityGroups`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxideaffinitygroup[$$OxideAffinityGroup$$] array__ | AffinityGroups contain the resolved groups that every instance launched from this nodeclass +
joins. It is only published when every selector resolved, so a group that has gone missing +
holds the previous set rather than silently shrinking it. +

This list is the desired set: the single source of truth for what a launch joins, what drift +
compares against, and what memberships are allowed to persist. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`storage`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-storagestatus[$$StorageStatus$$]__ | Storage is the resolved disk layout of a launched instance: the source each diskSet's disks are +
created from, and where each one lands in the guest. +

Published because several of these values are resolved rather than written -- the filesystem +
when the spec leaves it unset, and the mount point of each disk in a set with a mountDir -- so +
this is what makes the effective layout readable off the object rather than re-derived. It is +
also what a launch reads to decide which image or snapshot a data disk is created from, which +
is why it holds its previous value on an incomplete resolution rather than shrinking. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`bootstrap`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-bootstrapstatus[$$BootstrapStatus$$]__ | Bootstrap contains resolved state that only applies to a single bootstrap provider. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`conditions`* __link:https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/awslabs/operatorpkg/status#Condition[$$Condition$$] array__ | Conditions contains signals for health and readiness + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===

[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-snapshotselector"]
==== SnapshotSelector



SnapshotSelector selects a snapshot by ID or by name.

It has no OS or version term, unlike ImageSelector, because oxide.Snapshot has no such fields: a
snapshot in the Oxide API is an ID, a name, a project, the disk it came from, a size and a state,
and there is nothing else to match on.

Deliberately without CEL requiring exactly one of id/name, matching ImageSelector and the rest of
the selectors, which validate at reconcile instead.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-diskset[$$DiskSet$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`id`* __string__ | ID is the exact snapshot UUID. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`name`* __string__ | Name is the name of a snapshot. A name without a "*" must match exactly, ignoring case; a name +
containing "*" selects every snapshot whose name matches, where each "*" stands for any run of +
characters including none. Matched character by character, the same way an image name is. +

When a wildcard matches several snapshots the most recently created one is used. + |  | Optional: \{} +

| *`project`* __string__ | Project where the snapshot is located. Unlike an image, a snapshot is always in a project: +
there is no silo-level snapshot, so an empty project means the project Karpenter runs in. + |  | Optional: \{} +

|===


[id="{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-storage"]
==== Storage



Storage is the whole disk layout of a launched instance.

The 7-disk budget on diskSets is the Oxide attachment limit of 8 minus the boot disk. It is
checked here and again when a launch plans its disks: CEL refuses the edit, and the launch check
exists because CEL cannot be relied on to have run -- a nodeclass stored before this rule shipped
is not re-validated by the apiserver until it is next written.

The MaxItems on diskSets is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. The apiserver's CEL cost estimator
bounds all(), exists_one() and map() by the declared maximum list length, and the uniqueness rules
below are O(n^2); without a bound their estimated cost exceeds the per-rule budget and the CRD
fails to install.



.Appears In:
****
- xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-oxidenodeclassspec[$$OxideNodeClassSpec$$]
****

[cols="20a,50a,15a,15a", options="header"]
|===
| Field | Description | Default | Validation
| *`boot`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-bootdisk[$$BootDisk$$]__ | Boot is the disk the instance boots from. Its image comes from spec.imageSelector rather than +
from here: the boot image is what the whole nodeclass is built around, it is what +
nodeClaim.Status.ImageID records, and it is what image drift is decided on. + |  | Required: \{} +

| *`diskSets`* __xref:{anchor_prefix}-github-com-oxidecomputer-karpenter-provider-oxide-pkg-apis-v1alpha1-diskset[$$DiskSet$$] array__ | DiskSets are additional disks attached to every instance, in sets of identically configured +
disks. +

Order is not significant to what the guest sees, but it does decide the disk names, so +
reordering a nodeclass's diskSets changes the names of the disks the next launch creates. That +
is deliberately not drift: the names are internal and every launch renders its own, so the +
nodeclass hash is unchanged by a reorder even though the names are not. + |  | MaxItems: 7 +
Optional: \{} +

|===
